title: White Rice with Dark Green Vegetables, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice mixed with dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach or green beans) without any added fat. It is rich in carbohydrates, fiber, B‑vitamins and provides plant antioxidants from the vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll, which gives them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
The lack of added fat makes the dish low‑calorie, suitable for weight management.
Combining rice with vegetables offers a longer feeling of fullness by mixing fast and slow‑digesting carbs.
The recipe can be adapted to various cuisines by adding spices, soy sauce or herbs.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Dark green vegetables supply vitamin K, vitamin C, folate and potassium.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients in green vegetables help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, rice allergy can occur and requires avoidance of the product.

items.title: Lack of fat
items.content: Without fat, the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins from the vegetables may be reduced; consider adding a small amount of healthy fat elsewhere in the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a side or a standalone meal. It reheats well in the microwave; add soy sauce, lemon juice or fresh herbs for flavor. Pair with lean protein such as chicken, tofu or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it keeps for up to 2 months after cooling and placing in a freezer‑safe bag.
